wasm.reason: The canvas draws this catalog's components with a Compose Multiplatform build of Wear Compose — the Android AAR has no browser variant — so each is the component itself rather than an impression of it. What is still the canvas's own: the screen frame (the extent has no viewport for a real scaffold), the unrolled list (a long screenshot turns the row transformation off), and the type scale, which is the mobile theme's. Author on it; check a size on the Android preview, which compiles this design's own generated Kotlin against the real AAR.

native.reason: The generated Kotlin compiled against this module's own classpath and rendered under Robolectric: the same lane that produces this catalog's stickers.

frame.$comment_seedDevice: The first entry of catalog.spec.json's breakpoints table, named explicitly rather than defaulted: a new design opening at a size this catalog does not document would be drawn against padding nobody measured.

geometry.$comment: WRITTEN BY A TEST, NEVER BY HAND. catalog/src/test/kotlin/ee/schimke/wearm3catalog/ScreenScaffoldContentPaddingTest.kt composes the real ScreenScaffold over a real TransformingLazyColumn at each round size, reads the padding Wear Compose computes, and asserts this block equals its measurement. Editing these numbers is a failing test, which is the entire reason the block lives in this repository: the preview server carried a transcribed copy, and a number copied out of a render goes stale silently. ONLY WHAT THAT PROBE MEASURES IS HERE. The frame's corner radius, its sampled colours and its clock geometry are still constants in the server's renderer, sampled from this catalog's stitched capture; they move here when a probe measures them, and until then this catalog does not claim numbers it has not taken.

colorTokens.$comment: The theme roles a colour property or a background modifier may name — the vocabulary, not the values. A Wear design resolves these against Wear Material 3's own scheme, which is why the sampled colours the canvas draws the frame with are a separate question and still live in the server's renderer until a probe here measures them. The list itself is Material 3's, which Wear Material 3 shares: a design that names `onSurfaceVariant` means the same role on both, and on a watch it happens to be a warm #FFDCC2 rather than the grey a phone puts there.

Already absent from the component menu, so this entry changes nothing there; it is here to put the published reason on the record, which keeps every excluded component and carries the `excluded` string beside it.

Same exclusion, and the same reason, as `m3/sticker` in the sibling m3-catalog. The screen frame without a background fill. Published on `Progress indicators`.

wear-m3/wear-screen.excluded: the catalog's own preview frame, not a Wear Material 3 component: every sticker is drawn inside one, the Design Kit publishes no node for it, and nobody places one in a design. Same exclusion, and the same reason, as `m3/sticker` in the sibling m3-catalog. The list sections' screen frame — `MaterialTheme` plus an `AppScaffold` with a stubbed `TimeText`. It sits in a file that carries a `@file:CatalogGroup`, which is the only reason it published on a plausible-looking shelf (`Lists and screens`) rather than a scattered one.

wear-m3/media-row-sticker.excluded: the catalog's own preview frame, not a Wear Material 3 component: every sticker is drawn inside one, the Design Kit publishes no node for it, and nobody places one in a design. Same exclusion, and the same reason, as `m3/sticker` in the sibling m3-catalog. The Media Controls row frame — a `Sticker` narrowed to the kit's 192dp base screen width and a fixed row height. Same as `wear-screen`: its file's `@file:CatalogGroup` is why it published on `Media controls` rather than a scattered shelf.

Foundation, shared by Compose on both platforms — `androidx.compose.foundation` and `androidx.compose.ui` publish one of these, not two. It is the real component rather than a stand-in, which is why `wear-m3` shares it and shares no Material component at all.

properties.name: verticalArrangement
properties.notes: Distribution down the axis. The three aligned values compose with verticalSpacingDp through Arrangement.spacedBy(space, alignment); the three space* values distribute the free space themselves, and Compose has no form that also inserts a fixed gap.

properties.name: alignment
properties.notes: How a parent Box aligns this column. The renderer has always read `alignment` off any Box child and the exporter has always emitted `.align(...)` for it; only the declaration was missing, so a centred column was inexpressible.

properties.name: assetKey
properties.notes: The key of an asset the canvas can draw, written as {"type":"assetKey","value":"…"}: one of statusSemantics.assetRegistry.keys, or a key pinned in the design's own assets map by PUT /api/ui-builder/v1/designs/{designId}/assets/{assetKey} (raw PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP body) or the ui_builder_put_asset MCP tool. Any other key is refused at commit, so put the picture before inserting the node. A pinned key whose bytes this lane cannot show renders as a placeholder naming it, and exports as Image(painter = ColorPainter(...)) with an ASSET_PLACEHOLDER warning.

svg.notes: The recorder embeds the pinned asset bytes, or the project-owned artwork, with source and payload provenance; a key with no bytes behind it is drawn as a vector placeholder rather than declared as a raster fallback.
